Q: Git master branch has no upstream branch A:

As the error message suggests, you can use the following command to push the current branch and set the remote as upstream:

git push --set-upstream origin master

There's a config option that removes this ritual entirely (available since Git v2.37):

git config --global push.autoSetupRemote true

When it's enabled, Git assumes --set-upstream on the default push if no upstream tracking branch exists. It works with push.default set to simple (default since Git 2.0), current, or upstream. In a typical centralized workflow (same branch name locally and on origin), this means:

You create a branch → you push → tracking is set automatically.

Q: Git: fatal:The current branch XXX has no upstream branch (but it HAS the upstream branch) A:

To avoid seting upstream all the time, you can enable the push.autoSetupRemote config option (available in Git v2.37+):

git config --global push.autoSetupRemote true

When enabled, Git assumes --set-upstream on the default push if no upstream tracking branch exists. It works with push.default set to simple (default since Git 2.0), current, or upstream. In a typical centralized workflow (same branch name locally and on origin), this means:

You create a branch → you push → tracking is set automatically.
